claim: In teleost fish, altering the adult sex steroid milieu can effectively reverse sex-typical mating behaviors.
source: In teleost fish, altering the adult sex steroid milieu can effectively reverse sex-typical mating behaviors, suggesting remarkable sexual lability of their brains as adults.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established finding in the field.

claim: Neuropeptide B (NPB) is expressed female-specifically in the brain nuclei implicated in mating behavior in medaka.
source: In the teleost medaka, neuropeptide B (NPB) is expressed female-specifically in the brain nuclei implicated in mating behavior.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: NPB is a direct mediator of estrogen action on female mating behavior.
source: Here, we demonstrate that NPB is a direct mediator of estrogen action on female mating behavior, acting in a female-specific but reversible manner.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract and supported by multiple experiments throughout the manuscript.

claim: The female-specific expression of NPB is dependent on direct transcriptional activation by estrogen via an estrogen-responsive element.
source: Analysis of regulatory mechanisms revealed that the female-specific expression of NPB is dependent on direct transcriptional activation by estrogen via an estrogen-responsive element and is reversed in response to changes in the adult sex steroid milieu.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experiments with ΔERE mutants and hormone treatments.

claim: Female-specific NPB mediates female receptivity to male courtship.
source: Behavioral studies of NPB knockouts revealed that female-specific NBP mediates female receptivity to male courtship.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by behavioral analysis of knockout medaka.

claim: Estrogen and androgen receptors are expressed almost exclusively in females in Vs/Vp and PMm/PMg brain regions in medaka.
source: In the teleost species medaka (Oryzias latipes), we previously found that estrogen and androgen receptors are expressed almost exclusively in females in two brain regions: the supracommissural/posterior nucleus of the ventral telencephalic area (Vs/Vp) and the magnocellular/gigantocellular portion of the magnocellular preoptic nucleus (PMm/PMg) (Hiraki et al., 2012) (Figure 1A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to previous work.

claim: Vs/Vp and PMm/PMg are involved in mating behavior in teleosts.
source: This finding, together with classic lesion and stimulation studies suggesting that Vs/Vp and PMm/PMg are involved in mating behavior (Demski et al., 1975; Kyle and Peter, 1982; Koyama et al., 1984; Satou et al., 1984), led us to search for genes that are directly activated by estrogen and/or androgen in these brain regions and mediate female-typical mating behavior.
evidence: This is stated with citations to classic studies.

claim: npb expression in Vs/Vp and PMm/PMg is virtually confined to females and dependent on gonadal estrogen.
source: As a result, we identified a candidate gene, npb (encoding neuropeptide B; NPB), whose expression in Vs/Vp and PMm/PMg is virtually confined to females and dependent on gonadal estrogen (Hiraki et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to previous work.

claim: NPB and NPW were originally identified as ligands for the orphan receptors GPR7 and GPR8 (now designated NPBWR1 and NPBWR2).
source: NPB, together with its close relative, neuropeptide W (NPW), was originally identified as a ligand for the orphan receptors GPR7 and GPR8 (now designated NPBWR1 and NPBWR2) (Fujii et al., 2002; Brezillon et al., 2003; Tanaka et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated with citations to the original discovery papers.

claim: NPB and NPW have been implicated in food intake, energy homeostasis, inflammatory pain response, regulation of pituitary hormones, and social interaction.
source: NPB and NPW have been implicated in a wide array of physiological processes, including food intake, energy homeostasis, inflammatory pain response, regulation of pituitary hormones, and social interaction (Sakurai, 2013; Watanabe and Yamamoto, 2015); to our knowledge, however, there is no information regarding their role in mating behavior.
evidence: This is stated with citations to review articles.

claim: There is no prior information regarding the role of NPB/NPW in mating behavior.
source: NPB and NPW have been implicated in a wide array of physiological processes, including food intake, energy homeostasis, inflammatory pain response, regulation of pituitary hormones, and social interaction (Sakurai, 2013; Watanabe and Yamamoto, 2015); to our knowledge, however, there is no information regarding their role in mating behavior.
evidence: This is explicitly stated by the authors.

claim: Sex-reversed XY females exhibited the same high level of overall npba expression as wild-type XX females.
source: Real-time PCR performed on the whole brain revealed that sex-reversed XY females exhibited the same high level of overall npba expression as wild-type XX females, whereas sex-reversed XX males showed a much lower level of overall npba expression (p<0.0001 versus XX and XY females), comparable to that in wild-type XY males (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Sex-reversed XX males showed a much lower level of overall npba expression comparable to that in wild-type XY males.
source: Real-time PCR performed on the whole brain revealed that sex-reversed XY females exhibited the same high level of overall npba expression as wild-type XX females, whereas sex-reversed XX males showed a much lower level of overall npba expression (p<0.0001 versus XX and XY females), comparable to that in wild-type XY males (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The sexually dimorphic pattern of npba expression is independent of sex chromosome complement.
source: Thus, the sexually dimorphic pattern of npba expression is independent of sex chromosome complement, but linked to gonadal phenotype.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the sex-reversal experiments.

claim: The sexually dimorphic pattern of npba expression is linked to gonadal phenotype.
source: Thus, the sexually dimorphic pattern of npba expression is independent of sex chromosome complement, but linked to gonadal phenotype.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the sex-reversal experiments.

claim: ΔERE mutant females had a significantly lower level of overall npba expression compared with wild-type females.
source: Real-time PCR performed on the whole brain demonstrated that ΔERE mutant females had a significantly lower level of overall npba expression as compared with wild-type females (p<0.0001), whereas ΔERE mutant males had an even lower level (p<0.0001 versus wild-type and ΔERE mutant females), comparable to that in wild-type males (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: ΔERE mutant females showed a smaller total area of npba expression in Vs/Vp and PMm/PMg compared with wild-type females.
source: In agreement with these results, in situ hybridization analysis revealed a smaller total area of npba expression in Vs/Vp and PMm/PMg of ΔERE mutant females as compared with wild-type females (p=0.0202 for Vs/Vp, and 0.0058 for PMm/PMg) (Figure 1F), whereas npba expression in these nuclei was not detected in ΔERE or wild-type males.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: In ΔERE mutant females, npba expression was significantly reduced by ovariectomy and restored by E2 treatment, but E2 was not able to restore npba expression to the level present in wild-type females.
source: In the mutant female brain, npba expression was significantly reduced by ovariectomy and restored by E2 treatment, but E2 was not able to restore npba expression to the level present in wild-type females (p=0.0023 for the mutant versus wild-type females) (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Estrogen elicits the female-specific expression of npba by direct transcriptional activation through the ERE present in the npba promoter.
source: Taken together, these results demonstrate that estrogen elicits the female-specific expression of npba by direct transcriptional activation through the ERE present in the npba promoter, although other mechanisms are also likely involved in this estrogen effect.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the ΔERE mutant experiments.

claim: Other mechanisms besides direct ERE-mediated transcription are also likely involved in the estrogen effect on npba expression.
source: Taken together, these results demonstrate that estrogen elicits the female-specific expression of npba by direct transcriptional activation through the ERE present in the npba promoter, although other mechanisms are also likely involved in this estrogen effect.
evidence: This is stated as a caveat to the main conclusion.

claim: ∆ERE mutant females had brain levels of E2 comparable to those of wild-type females.
source: The possibility that decreased npba expression in ∆ERE mutant females was due to a decrease in estrogen levels in their brains was ruled out by the observation that ∆ERE mutant females had brain levels of E2 comparable to those of wild-type females (p=0.782) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Treating castrated males with E2 induced npba expression in both Vs/Vp and PMm/PMg.
source: Indeed, in situ hybridization results showed that treating castrated males with E2 induced npba expression in both Vs/Vp and PMm/PMg (p=0.0013 for Vs/Vp and 0.0006 for PMm/PMg) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Treating ovary-intact adult females continuously with 11-ketotestosterone (KT) caused a gradual decline in npba expression in Vs/Vp.
source: In situ hybridization results showed that treating ovary-intact adult females continuously with 11-ketotestosterone (KT; the most prominent, non-aromatizable androgen in teleosts) caused a gradual decline in npba expression in Vs/Vp, decreasing both the number of npba-expressing neurons (p<0.0001 on days 5 and 9) and the total area of npba expression (p=0.0002 on day 2; p<0.0001 on days 5 and 9) to undetectable or nearly undetectable levels over the treatment period (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2A–C.

claim: Treating ovary-intact adult females with an aromatase inhibitor (AI) caused a decline in npba expression in Vs/Vp.
source: Treating ovary-intact adult females with an aromatase inhibitor (AI; aromatase converts androgen to estrogen) yielded essentially the same results (p<0.0001 for number of neurons in Vs/Vp on days 2, 5, and 9; p=0.0063 and 0.0025 for total area in Vs/Vp on days 5 and 9, respectively; p=0.0108 for total area in PMm/PMg on day 9) (Figure 2D–F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2D–F.

claim: E2 levels in the brain of KT-treated females fell to less than 5% of untreated controls within 2 days and remained low during the remainder of the treatment period.
source: The results showed that E2 levels fell to less than 5% of untreated controls within 2 days and remained low during the remainder of the treatment period (p<0.0001 on days 2, 5, and 9), demonstrating a substantial decrease in E2 levels in the brain of KT-treated females (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Treating testis-intact adult males continuously with E2 resulted in the induction of npba expression in both Vs/Vp and PMm/PMg.
source: In contrast, treating testis-intact adult males continuously with E2 resulted in the induction of npba expression in both Vs/Vp and PMm/PMg, where both the number of npba-expressing neurons and the total area of npba expression steadily increased over time during treatment (p<0.0001 for number of neurons in Vs/Vp on days 2, 5, and 9; p=0.0013 and<0.0001 for total area in Vs/Vp on days 5 and 9, respectively; p<0.0001 for number of neurons in PMm/PMg on day 9; p=0.0023 for total area in PMm/PMg on day 9) (Figure 2G–I).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2G–I.

claim: The sexually dimorphic pattern of npba expression can be reversed in both directions in response to changes in the sex steroid milieu.
source: Thus, the sexually dimorphic pattern of npba expression can be reversed in both directions in response to changes in the sex steroid milieu.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the hormone treatment experiments.

claim: The anti-Npba antibody selectively identified neurons expressing the npba transcript.
source: The specificity of the anti-Npba antibody was ascertained by a double-labeling experiment with immunohistochemistry and in situ hybridization, where it selectively identified neurons expressing the npba transcript (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The anti-Npba antibody does not cross-react with Npbb.
source: In addition, this antibody was found not to cross-react with Npbb as confirmed by the complete absence of labeling with this antibody in npba knockout females (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: npba is expressed in both sexes in several brain nuclei, including Pbl in the ventrolateral preoptic area.
source: Although the focus of the present study is female-specific subsets of npba-expressing neurons in Vs/Vp and PMm/PMg and these neurons account for a large proportion of overall npba expression in the female brain, npba is expressed in both sexes in several brain nuclei, including Pbl in the ventrolateral preoptic area (Hiraki et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to previous work.

claim: Npba-immunoreactive axons arising from the neuronal cell bodies in Pbl and extending through the hypothalamus into the pituitary were observed in both sexes.
source: Consistent with this fact, Npba-immunoreactive axons arising from the neuronal cell bodies in Pbl and extending through the hypothalamus into the pituitary were observed in both sexes (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by images shown in Figure 3A.

claim: In females, additional Npba-immunoreactive axons were found in many areas of the central nervous system, with particular abundance in the thalamus, hypothalamus, optic tectum, midbrain tegmentum, medulla oblongata, and spinal cord.
source: In females, additional Npba-immunoreactive axons were found in many areas of the central nervous system, with particular abundance in the thalamus, hypothalamus, optic tectum, midbrain tegmentum, medulla oblongata, and spinal cord (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by images shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The distribution of GFP and endogenous npba transcripts almost completely overlapped in npba-GFP transgenic medaka.
source: The specificity of GFP expression was confirmed by double in situ hybridization detecting GFP and endogenous npba transcripts, which demonstrated that the distribution of the two transcripts almost completely overlapped (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: The female-specific axons in npba-GFP transgenic medaka reached the posterior end of the spinal cord.
source: In addition, imaging of whole brains and spinal cords revealed that the female-specific axons reached the posterior end of the spinal cord and that all female-specific axons most probably originated from the female-specific npba-expressing neurons in Vs/Vp and PMm/PMg.
evidence: This is stated based on imaging of transgenic fish.

claim: All female-specific axons most probably originated from the female-specific npba-expressing neurons in Vs/Vp and PMm/PMg.
source: In addition, imaging of whole brains and spinal cords revealed that the female-specific axons reached the posterior end of the spinal cord and that all female-specific axons most probably originated from the female-specific npba-expressing neurons in Vs/Vp and PMm/PMg.
evidence: This is stated as a probable conclusion based on imaging data.

claim: A large number of npba-expressing neurons were widely scattered over the medulla oblongata and spinal cord, and all of these subsets of neurons were common to both sexes.
source: Although a large number of npba-expressing neurons were widely scattered over the medulla oblongata and spinal cord, all of these subsets of neurons were common to both sexes and were not confined to, or predominant in, females (Figure 3—figure supplement 3), thereby showing that the female-specific axons did not originate from these regions.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: The female-specific axons did not originate from the medulla oblongata or spinal cord.
source: Although a large number of npba-expressing neurons were widely scattered over the medulla oblongata and spinal cord, all of these subsets of neurons were common to both sexes and were not confined to, or predominant in, females (Figure 3—figure supplement 3), thereby showing that the female-specific axons did not originate from these regions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the in situ hybridization data.

claim: The isolated medaka cDNA encoded a protein orthologous to NPBWR2 and paralogous to NPBWR1 of other species.
source: Phylogenetic tree analysis demonstrated that this cDNA encoded a medaka protein orthologous to NPBWR2 and paralogous to NPBWR1 of other species (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by phylogenetic analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: NPBWR1 is absent in medaka as in zebrafish.
source: No other NPBWR1/NPBWR2-like genes were found in our EST library or public medaka genome/EST databases, indicating the absence of NPBWR1 in medaka as in zebrafish (Danio rerio) (Bu et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated based on database searches and cited work in zebrafish.

claim: npbwr2 is expressed in multiple brain nuclei and spinal cord regions in both males and females.
source: In situ hybridization identified npbwr2 expression in the following nuclei in both males and females: Vv, Vl, and Vs/Vp in the ventral telencephalon; Dm/Dl in the dorsal telencephalon; PMp, PPa, and PPp in the preoptic area, rHd and lHd in the habenula; VM and DP/CP in the thalamus; PGZ3 in the optic tectum; NDLI, NAT, NVT, NRL, NPT, and NRP in the hypothalamus; IR/MR/IQ and DT/TS/is in the midbrain tegmentum; ra and gc/RS in the brain stem; the peripheral region of the anterior pituitary; and the medial part of the dorsal horn and the lateral part of the ventral horn throughout the spinal cord (Figure 3D; abbreviations of brain and spinal cord regions and brain nuclei are defined in Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: There were no overt differences in the distribution pattern of npbwr2 expression between the sexes.
source: There were no overt differences in the distribution pattern of npbwr2 expression between the sexes.
evidence: This is stated based on in situ hybridization analysis.

claim: Npba that is produced female-specifically in Vs/Vp and PMm/PMg is transported to and acts in many different brain areas and the spinal cord.
source: Collectively, these results suggest that Npba that is produced female-specifically in Vs/Vp and PMm/PMg is transported to and acts in many different brain areas and the spinal cord.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the axonal projection and receptor expression data.

claim: Medaka possess an additional NPB gene, designated npbb.
source: Via a survey of the medaka genome and EST databases, we identified a previously uncharacterized gene encoding a protein highly homologous to, but distinct from, Npba.
evidence: This is stated based on database searches and sequence analysis.

claim: The two NPB genes arose from the whole-genome duplication that occurred early in teleost evolution.
source: These lines of evidence strongly suggest that the two NPB genes arose from the whole-genome duplication that occurred early in teleost evolution (Amores et al., 1998).
evidence: This is stated based on comparative synteny analysis and cited work on teleost genome duplication.

claim: NPW is absent in medaka as in zebrafish.
source: No other NPB/NPW-like genes were found in our EST library or public medaka genome/EST databases, indicating the absence of NPW in medaka as in zebrafish (Bu et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated based on database searches and cited work in zebrafish.

claim: Both Npba and Npbb dose-dependently activated medaka Npbwr2, resulting in a decrease in intracellular cAMP levels.
source: Receptor activation assays revealed that both Npba and Npbb dose-dependently activated medaka Npbwr2, resulting in a decrease in intracellular cAMP levels, as reported for NPBWR1/2 of other species (Fujii et al., 2002; Tanaka et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated based on receptor activation assays and cited work in other species.

claim: Npbb displayed greater potency than Npba with a 50% inhibitory concentration (IC50) of 4.3 nM versus 240 nM.
source: Npbb displayed greater potency than Npba with a 50% inhibitory concentration (IC50) of 4.3 nM versus 240 nM (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Males had slightly higher levels of npbb expression in the optic tectum than females.
source: Expression of npbb was observed in all three parts, but was highest in the optic tectum, where males had slightly higher levels than females (p=0.014) (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: A marked difference between the sexes was observed in Vs/Vp, where npbb expression was observed in females, but completely absent in males.
source: A marked difference between the sexes was observed in Vs/Vp (p<0.0001), where npbb expression was observed in females, but completely absent in males (Figure 4D,F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 4D,F.

claim: npbb-expressing neurons in PMm/PMg/PPp were more abundant in number and displayed a much larger total area of expression in females than in males.
source: Similarly, npbb-expressing neurons in PMm/PMg/PPp were more abundant in number and displayed a much larger total area of expression in females than in males (p=0.0011 for number of neurons; p<0.0001 for total area) (Figure 4D–F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 4D–F.

claim: npba and npbb are expressed in the same subset of neurons within Vs/Vp and PMm/PMg/PPp.
source: The simultaneous detection of npba and npbb expression showed that these genes are expressed in the same subset of neurons within Vs/Vp and PMm/PMg/PPp; in contrast, no neurons in other brain nuclei were found to express both genes (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: No neurons in brain nuclei other than Vs/Vp and PMm/PMg/PPp were found to express both npba and npbb.
source: The simultaneous detection of npba and npbb expression showed that these genes are expressed in the same subset of neurons within Vs/Vp and PMm/PMg/PPp; in contrast, no neurons in other brain nuclei were found to express both genes (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: In adult females, ovariectomy caused a significant reduction in npbb expression in both Vs/Vp and PMm/PMg/PPp, which was restored by treatment with E2 but not by KT.
source: In adult females, ovariectomy caused a significant reduction in npbb expression in both Vs/Vp (p=0.0271) and PMm/PMg/PPp (p=0.0041), which was restored by treatment with E2 (p=0.0091 for Vs/Vp, and 0.0173 for PMm/PMg) but not by KT (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: In adult males, E2 treatment following castration induced a few npbb-expressing neurons in Vs/Vp.
source: In adult males, E2 treatment following castration induced a few npbb-expressing neurons in Vs/Vp (p<0.0001), whereas npbb expression in PMm/PMg/PPp did not show clear responses to any treatment (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Both KT and AI treatment of ovary-intact adult females resulted in a gradual decline in npbb expression in Vs/Vp.
source: Both KT and AI treatment of ovary-intact adult females resulted in a gradual decline in npbb expression in Vs/Vp, both in the number of npbb-expressing neurons and in the total area of npbb expression, to undetectable or nearly undetectable levels (p<0.0001 for number of neurons in KT-treated fish on days 5 and 9; p=0.0235,<0.0001, and <0.0001 for total area in KT-treated fish on days 2, 5, and 9, respectively; p=0.0002 and<0.0001 for number of neurons in AI-treated fish on days 5 and 9, respectively; p=0.0013 and 0.0009 for total area in AI-treated fish on days 5 and 9, respectively) (Figure 5A–F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 5A–F.

claim: KT treatment, but not AI treatment, led to a significant decrease in npbb expression in PMm/PMg/PPp.
source: KT treatment, but not AI treatment, also led to a significant decrease in npbb expression in PMm/PMg/PPp (p=0.0038 for number of neurons in KT-treated fish on day 9; p=0.0021 and<0.0001 for total area in KT-treated fish on days 5 and 9, respectively) (Figure 5A–F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 5A–F.

claim: E2 treatment of testis-intact adult males caused a few npbb-expressing neurons to be newly induced in Vs/Vp.
source: E2 treatment of testis-intact adult males caused no clear changes in npbb expression in either Vs/Vp or PMm/PMg/PPp, but a few npbb-expressing neurons were newly induced in Vs/Vp (p=0.0369) (Figure 5G–I).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 5G–I.

claim: The sexually dimorphic pattern of npbb expression can be reversed, at least in part, in response to changes in the sex steroid milieu.
source: Collectively, these results show that, similar to npba expression, the sexually dimorphic pattern of npbb expression can be reversed, at least in part, in response to changes in the sex steroid milieu.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the hormone treatment experiments.

claim: The npbb promoter in medaka contains a putative ERE at a similar position as in the npba promoter.
source: Search for putative EREs in the npbb promoter led us to identify a putative ERE at a similar position as in the npba promoter.
evidence: This is stated based on computational analysis of the promoter sequence.

claim: The npb promoter in gar and the npba/npbb promoters in several teleost species contain a putative ERE at a similar position.
source: In addition, the npb promoter in gar and the npba/npbb promoters in several teleost species examined were also found to contain a putative ERE at a similar position (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: Most homozygous females of both npba-/- and npbb-/- knockout strains spawned successfully, similar to wild-type and heterozygous females.
source: Most homozygous females of both knockout strains spawned successfully, similar to wild-type and heterozygous females.
evidence: This is stated based on behavioral observations.

claim: npba-/- females showed a significant increase in latencies from the first courtship display to the first wrapping and to the wrapping that resulted in spawning compared with npba+/+ and npba+/- females.
source: Here, we found a significant increase in latencies from the first courtship display to the first wrapping and to the wrapping that resulted in spawning for npba-/- females as compared with npba+/+ and npba+/- females (p=0.0256 and 0.0002, respectively, for the latency to the first wrapping; p=0.0104 and 0.0026, respectively, for the latency to the wrapping that resulted in spawning) (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: npbb-/- females compared with controls showed no significant difference in any of the behavioral parameters.
source: In contrast, npbb-/- females compared with controls showed no significant difference in any of the behavioral parameters (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Homozygous females, as well as males, of both npba-/-/npbb-/- and npbwr2-/- strains were found to be fertile, sexually active, and to spawn successfully.
source: Homozygous females, as well as males, of both strains were found to be fertile, sexually active, and to spawn successfully.
evidence: This is stated based on behavioral observations.

claim: A significant increase in the latency from the first courtship display to the first wrapping was observed for both npba-/-/npbb-/- and npbwr2-/- females as compared with wild-type females.
source: However, as was the case with npba-/- females, a significant increase in the latency from the first courtship display to the first wrapping was observed for both npba-/-/npbb-/- and npbwr2-/- females as compared with wild-type females (p=0.0064 for npba-/-/npbb-/-, and 0.0002 for npbwr2-/-) (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: npbwr2-/- females showed a significant increase in latency from the first courtship display to the wrapping that resulted in spawning.
source: npbwr2-/- females also showed a significant increase in latency from the first courtship display to the wrapping that resulted in spawning (p=0.0013) (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: There was a significant increase in the proportion of females that spawned without any preceding courtship display from the male for both npba-/-/npbb-/- and npbwr2-/- strains.
source: In addition, there was a significant increase in the proportion of females that spawned without any preceding courtship display from the male for both npba-/-/npbb-/- (p=0.0405) and npbwr2-/- (p=0.0010) strains (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: NPB signaling affects female receptivity to male courtship.
source: Collectively, these results indicate that NPB signaling affects female receptivity to male courtship.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the behavioral analysis of knockout medaka.

claim: NPB signaling constitutes a female-specific but reversible component of the female sexual receptivity pathway.
source: The present results indicate that NPB signaling constitutes a female-specific but reversible component of the female sexual receptivity pathway.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the discussion.

claim: The sexually dimorphic pattern of npba expression is independent of sex chromosome complement, and relies exclusively on gonadal sex steroids.
source: Here, however, we found that the sexually dimorphic pattern of npba expression is independent of sex chromosome complement, and relies exclusively on gonadal sex steroids.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the discussion.

claim: The lack of sex chromosome effects underlies the reversibility of the sexually dimorphic npba expression.
source: The lack of sex chromosome effects certainly underlies the reversibility of the sexually dimorphic npba expression.
evidence: This is stated as an inference in the discussion.

claim: Female-specific npba-expressing neurons coexpress estrogen receptors (ERs).
source: Consistent with this, female-specific npba-expressing neurons coexpress estrogen receptors (ERs) (Hiraki et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to previous work.

claim: Very few genes involved in female mating behavior in any species have been found to be direct targets of estrogen.
source: The identification of npba as a direct target of estrogen action is interesting because very few genes involved in female mating behavior in any species have been found to be direct targets of estrogen, although such genes can be highly estrogen-responsive (Yang and Shah, 2014).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to a review article.

claim: The genes encoding the progesterone receptor, oxytocin, and oxytocin receptor are expressed in behaviorally relevant brain regions of both males and females, and affect the mating behaviors of both sexes.
source: The exceptions are the genes encoding the progesterone receptor, oxytocin, and oxytocin receptor; however, those genes are expressed in behaviorally relevant brain regions of both males and females, and affect the mating behaviors of both sexes, in contrast to npba in medaka (Wagner, 2006; Yang et al., 2013; Veening et al., 2015; Dumais and Veenema, 2016; Pfaff et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated with citations to multiple papers.

claim: The female-specific expression of npba has a distinct regulatory mechanism.
source: Collectively, our findings indicate that the female-specific expression of npba has a distinct regulatory mechanism.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the discussion.

claim: In mice, the cholecystokinin receptor gene (Cckar) implicated in female sexual receptivity is expressed in the ventromedial nucleus of the hypothalamus at much higher levels in females owing to estrogen stimulation.
source: In mice, for example, the cholecystokinin receptor gene (Cckar) implicated in female sexual receptivity is expressed in the ventromedial nucleus of the hypothalamus at much higher levels in females owing to estrogen stimulation.
evidence: This is stated as an example from the literature.

claim: Although Cckar expression in the ventromedial nucleus is reduced by ovariectomy and reinstated by treatment with estrogen in adult females, treating adult males with estrogen does not induce expression of Cckar in this nucleus.
source: Although Cckar expression in this nucleus is reduced by ovariectomy and reinstated by treatment with estrogen in adult females, treating adult males with estrogen does not induce expression of Cckar in this nucleus (Xu et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to a specific paper.

claim: Perinatal sex steroids have long-lasting or even permanent effects on brain gene expression and behavior via epigenetic mechanisms involving DNA methylation and histone modifications.
source: Studies in rodents indicate that perinatal sex steroids have long-lasting or even permanent effects on brain gene expression and behavior via epigenetic mechanisms involving DNA methylation and histone modifications, which establish and maintain differences between the sexes across the lifespan (McCarthy and Nugent, 2015; Forger et al., 2016; McCarthy et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated with citations to review articles.

claim: The reversible sex difference in adult npba expression in medaka suggests either that perinatal sex steroids induce few, if any, epigenetic modifications in npba or that such modifications can easily be reversed for some reason.
source: The reversible sex difference in adult npba expression in medaka suggests either that perinatal sex steroids induce few, if any, epigenetic modifications in npba or that such modifications can easily be reversed for some reason.
evidence: This is stated as an inference in the discussion.

claim: This unique mode of sexual differentiation of npba expression probably contributes to the adult reversal of sex-typical mating behaviors observed in teleosts.
source: This unique mode of sexual differentiation of npba expression probably contributes to the adult reversal of sex-typical mating behaviors observed in teleosts.
evidence: This is stated as a probable conclusion in the discussion.

claim: Behavior-relevant genes for which expression in the adult brain is sexually dimorphic but bidirectionally reversible in response to sex steroids may remain to be identified in mammals and birds.
source: Given that mammals and birds also exhibit some degree of sexual lability in mating behavior, behavior-relevant genes for which expression in the adult brain is sexually dimorphic but bidirectionally reversible in response to sex steroids may remain to be identified.
evidence: This is stated as speculation in the discussion.

claim: Androgen/androgen receptor (AR) signaling plays an inhibitory role in npba expression, alongside the stimulatory role of estrogen/ER signaling.
source: The profound decrease in npba expression observed in ovary-intact females treated with non-aromatizable androgen indicates that androgen/androgen receptor (AR) signaling plays an inhibitory role in npba expression, alongside the stimulatory role of estrogen/ER signaling.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the discussion.

claim: The androgen/AR signaling does not directly inhibit npba expression.
source: However, expression of npba was not induced in males deprived of androgen by castration, suggesting that the androgen/AR signaling does not directly inhibit npba expression.
evidence: This is stated as an inference in the discussion.

claim: The androgen/AR signaling pathway presumably exerts its influence by attenuating the stimulatory action of estrogen through a reduction of brain E2 levels.
source: Considering a concomitant decrease in brain levels of E2 in androgen-treated males, the androgen/AR signaling pathway presumably exerts its influence by attenuating the stimulatory action of estrogen through a reduction of brain E2 levels.
evidence: This is stated as a presumption in the discussion.

claim: The inhibitory action of androgen on npba expression may involve repression of estrogen/ER signaling not only at ligand, but also at receptor level.
source: Given that ER expression in Vs/Vp and PMp/PMg is strongly suppressed by androgen (Hiraki et al., 2012), the inhibitory action of androgen on npba expression may involve repression of estrogen/ER signaling not only at ligand, but also at receptor level.
evidence: This is stated as a possibility in the discussion with a citation to previous work.

claim: Treating males with estrogen induces ER expression in Vs/Vp and PMm/PMg.
source: However, we previously found that ERs are not expressed at detectable levels in Vs/Vp and PMm/PMg of males and that treating males with estrogen induces ER expression therein (Hiraki et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to previous work.

claim: The estrogen-induced npba expression in males is not fully realized until sufficient ER expression is achieved.
source: Considering these findings, it seems plausible that this estrogen-induced npba expression is not fully realized until sufficient ER expression is achieved.
evidence: This is stated as a plausible explanation in the discussion.

claim: The Npba-expressing neurons emerged in adult males treated with estrogen, not through neurogenesis, but through the activation of pre-existing, quiescent male counterpart neurons.
source: However, our recent work showed that the Npba-expressing neurons emerged in adult males treated with estrogen, not through neurogenesis, but through the activation of pre-existing, quiescent male counterpart neurons (Kikuchi et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to recent work.

claim: An activation–inactivation process on existing neurons, rather than neurogenesis, is relevant in the reversible sexual dimorphism in npba expression.
source: This evidence suggests the relevance of an activation–inactivation process on existing neurons, rather than neurogenesis, in the reversible sexual dimorphism in npba expression.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the discussion.

claim: Most of the isotocin neurons that are intermingled with the female-specific npba-expressing neurons in PMm/PMg project to the pituitary in teleosts including medaka.
source: The latter observation is surprising, given that most of the isotocin neurons that are intermingled with the female-specific npba-expressing neurons in PMm/PMg project to the pituitary in teleosts including medaka (Hiraki et al., 2014; Yamashita et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous work.

claim: In the spinal cord, npbwr2 was expressed in the medial part of the dorsal horn and the lateral part of the ventral horn, which respectively contain sympathetic preganglionic neurons and motoneurons in teleosts as well as in mammals.
source: In the spinal cord, npbwr2 was expressed in the medial part of the dorsal horn and the lateral part of the ventral horn, which respectively contain sympathetic preganglionic neurons and motoneurons in teleosts as well as in mammals (Westerfield et al., 1986; Schneider and Sulner, 2006; Funakoshi and Nakano, 2007).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous work.

claim: The female-specific Npba probably acts on either or both sympathetic preganglionic neurons and motoneurons in the spinal cord.
source: Thus, the female-specific Npba probably acts on either or both of these neurons in the spinal cord, as well as in various neuronal subsets in the brain.
evidence: This is stated as a probable conclusion in the discussion.

claim: NPBWR1/2 primarily couples to the inhibitory G protein (Gi).
source: Although NPBWR1/2 primarily couples to the inhibitory G protein (Gi) (Fujii et al., 2002; Tanaka et al., 2003), activation of NPBWR1 reportedly leads to increased excitability of some neuronal populations in rats (Price et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous work.

claim: Activation of NPBWR1 reportedly leads to increased excitability of some neuronal populations in rats.
source: Although NPBWR1/2 primarily couples to the inhibitory G protein (Gi) (Fujii et al., 2002; Tanaka et al., 2003), activation of NPBWR1 reportedly leads to increased excitability of some neuronal populations in rats (Price et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to previous work.

claim: npbb probably originated from the teleost-specific whole-genome duplication and is thus confined to teleosts.
source: Phylogenetic and syntenic analyses indicated that this gene probably originated from the teleost-specific whole-genome duplication (Amores et al., 1998) and is thus confined to teleosts.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the discussion with a citation.

claim: npba and npbb share common regulatory mechanisms.
source: Similar to npba, npbb was found to be preferentially expressed in females in Vs/Vp and PMm/PMg/PPp; in addition, npba and npbb were expressed in the same neurons in these brain nuclei, suggesting that the two genes share common regulatory mechanisms.
evidence: This is stated as a suggestion in the discussion.

claim: A cis-regulatory region that confers estrogen-responsive NPB gene expression is evolutionary conserved.
source: In addition, a putative ERE, though not yet proven to be functional, was found in the npbb promoter at a similar position as in the npba promoter, suggesting that npbb is also directly activated by estrogen and that a cis-regulatory region that confers estrogen-responsive NPB gene expression is evolutionary conserved.
evidence: This is stated as a suggestion in the discussion.

claim: The two genes npba and npbb have a shared function in female mating behavior.
source: The results also suggested that the two genes have a shared function in female mating behavior; indeed, part of the altered behavioral phenotypes was evident in npba-/-/npbb-/- females, but not in single knockouts of either of the two genes, presumably due to functional redundancy.
evidence: This is stated as a suggestion in the discussion.

claim: Coexpression of npba and npbb was observed exclusively in Vs/Vp and PMm/PMg/PPp and not in other brain nuclei, which strongly suggests that their expression in these nuclei is responsible for the phenotypes observed.
source: Importantly, coexpression of npba and npbb was observed exclusively in Vs/Vp and PMm/PMg/PPp and not in other brain nuclei, which strongly suggests that their expression in these nuclei is responsible for the phenotypes observed.
evidence: This is stated as a strong suggestion in the discussion.

claim: The deficiency of NPB signaling reduces the significance of courtship display in female receptivity.
source: The most likely explanation is that the deficiency of NPB signaling reduces the significance of courtship display in female receptivity.
evidence: This is stated as the most likely explanation in the discussion.

claim: Courtship display is somehow less important and less effective for females deficient in NPB signaling.
source: Conceivably, courtship display is somehow less important and less effective for females deficient in NPB signaling; in other words, they require more time to accept males after receiving courtship stimulation, but simultaneously tend to accept males without being courted.
evidence: This is stated as a conceivable explanation in the discussion.

claim: Female-specific NPB signaling may play an important role in female mate choice by facilitating the acceptance of males performing courtship display and the refusal of males exhibiting no courtship.
source: Thus, female-specific NPB signaling may play an important role in female mate choice by facilitating the acceptance of males performing courtship display and the refusal of males exhibiting no courtship.
evidence: This is stated as a possible role in the discussion.

claim: Npbwr1-/- mice exhibit behavioral abnormalities in social interaction: when confronted by a conspecific intruder, they approach rapidly and spend more time close to the intruder.
source: The answer remains to be found, but Npbwr1-/- mice have been shown to exhibit behavioral abnormalities in social interaction: when confronted by a conspecific intruder, they approach rapidly and spend more time close to the intruder (Nagata-Kuroiwa et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to previous work.

claim: A single nucleotide polymorphism in human NPBWR1 has been shown to influence the evaluation of facial expressions.
source: In addition, a single nucleotide polymorphism in human NPBWR1 has been shown to influence the evaluation of facial expressions (Watanabe et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to previous work.

claim: NPB signaling may be involved in the process of perceiving and/or evaluating male performance during courtship.
source: These observations, together with the extensive effective area of female-specific NPB signaling in the brain, suggest that NPB signaling may be involved in the process of perceiving and/or evaluating male performance during courtship.
evidence: This is stated as a suggestion in the discussion.

claim: NPB signaling, by influencing motor and/or sympathetic function, may be involved in executing the decision of whether or not to mate.
source: Alternatively, given that the spinal cord is the major target site of female-specific NPB signaling, it is possible that NPB signaling, by influencing motor and/or sympathetic function, may be involved in executing the decision of whether or not to mate.
evidence: This is stated as an alternative possibility in the discussion.

claim: The female-specific NPB neurons are located in Vs/Vp and PMm/PMg, regions that are considered homologous to the bed nucleus of the stria terminalis/subpallial amygdala and the supraoptic nucleus/paraventricular nucleus, respectively, in the mammalian brain.
source: In summary, the present study has identified NPB as a critical element of the female sexual receptivity circuitry in medaka, exhibiting reversible sexual dimorphism under the direct control of estrogen. The female-specific NPB neurons are located in Vs/Vp and PMm/PMg, regions that are considered homologous to the bed nucleus of the stria terminalis/subpallial amygdala and the supraoptic nucleus/paraventricular nucleus, respectively, in the mammalian brain (Northcutt, 1995; Moore and Lowry, 1998; O'Connell and Hofmann, 2011; Goodson and Kingsbury, 2013).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous work.

claim: NPB/NPW neurons have been detected in the bed nucleus of the stria terminalis/subpallial amygdala and the supraoptic nucleus/paraventricular nucleus in mammals.
source: Similar to medaka, NPB/NPW neurons have been detected in these nuclei in mammals (Dun et al., 2003; Jackson et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated with citations to previous work.

claim: The role of NPB in female sexual receptivity may be conserved across a wide array of vertebrate taxa.
source: Thus, the role of NPB in female sexual receptivity may be conserved across a wide array of vertebrate taxa.
evidence: This is stated as a possibility in the discussion.
